pageCache.text:
Welcome
Devonshire House is a co-educational prep school, for girls and boys aged 2-13, offering unparalleled preparation for senior school and life thereafter. Our unwavering focus on individual growth, within an inclusive community, blends traditional values and modern practice to inspire fearless life-long learning.
Head’s Welcome
At Devonshire House, we occupy a rare midground: academic rigour and a happy, balanced, nurturing childhood. Your child will fly academically precisely because they are known and loved as an individual through bespoke relationships.
Growth
Wonder
Courage
Belonging
Get to know our School
Tour the school and you will meet nice kids – confident but humble, bright and engaged, thoughtful and curious, comfortable in their own skin as they show you around.
Ask parents what they prize about Devonshire House, and they will point to happy children, a diverse and inclusive community, shared values, and a truly personalised approach to learning.
Talk to teachers and you’ll be struck by their energy, their warmth, their passion for individual growth and their unerring commitment to helping your child succeed.
ABOUT US OPEN MORNINGS
The School Signature…
…through our elite collaboration with Tottenham Hotspur Football Club.
“…a solid, stretching, well-connected prep school of the highest standard, offering something for everybody aged 2 to 13.”
Admissions
Whilst our senior school success will speak to the head, the heart will only know as you start to get under the skin of the school through the admissions process. Talk to us about your child. Soak up the school spirit. Ask all the questions. Imagine your family here.
© Devonshire House 2026
The best way to get to know our school is to visit one of our Open Mornings!

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us | Devonshire House Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Our Mission
We exist to grow upstanding people equipped to navigate their future. People, not pupils; upstanders, not bystanders. We develop empathetic, resilient, thoughtful and curious humans, alive to their talents and passions. By equipping them to take their place in our diverse world with self-awareness and integrity, we empower them to navigate their future with confidence, compassion and commitment.
Growth
Wonder
Courage
Belonging
10 reasons to choose Devonshire House
1. Co-educational
Devonshire House is a co-educational school which caters for the whole family, welcoming children from 2-13.
2. Springboard to a range of reputable senior schools
Intimate knowledge of your child and the senior school landscape means we consistently secure places at preferred schools.
3. Belonging for all
We are a diverse, non-denominational and inclusive community, reflective of our location in a global city. Yet the warmth of the community spirit has a village feel, bringing belonging, connection and a network for the whole family.
4. Academic excellence AND nurture
Our academic excellence and fearless love of learning is underpinned by shared values and a long-established culture of wellbeing. You don’t have to choose between an academically rigorous and pastorally nurturing school; the two go hand in hand here.
5. Professional leadership
You have the peace of mind which strong leadership from an experienced and well-connected Head brings, underpinned by the quality, investment, security and training of belonging to the Dukes Governance family of schools.
6. Space to be a child
Thanks to a variety of outdoor spaces, including a forest school, your child will have the space to explore, let off steam and experience the well-documented boost to wellbeing from being outside.
7. A place to find your spark
Our specialist teachers and facilities provide exceptional co-curricular opportunities across the board. Your child will be able to discover what makes them feel alive, whether that’s creative expression through the arts, playing sport or contributing to society via the eco-club or the charity committee.
8. Preparation for life
We focus on world-readiness from a young age: learning how to function in society; seeing and becoming positive role models; developing leadership skills; forging confidence.
9. Flexibility for working parents
You have the flexibility of an extended day and holiday clubs, aided by our location in the heart of Hampstead with ready access to transport links.
10. Partnership & communication
We understand the enormity of entrusting your child to school. We believe that it takes a village to raise a child and promote partnership, transparency and two-way communication.
“…a solid, stretching, well-connected prep school of the highest standard, offering something for everybody aged 2 to 13.”
© Devonshire House 2026
The best way to get to know our school is to visit one of our Open Mornings!

pageCache.pageTitle: Head's Welcome | Devonshire House Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Introducing Mrs O’Brien – New Head of School from September 2026
Previously Head of School at St Michael’s in Highgate, I have spent over 20 years working in North London primary schools. 10 years of those were as a Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCo), a role that has deepened my commitment to ensuring every child feels supported, valued, and able to achieve their very best.
I care deeply about providing high-quality teaching and creating a school environment where children feel happy, confident, and inspired to learn. I believe that when pupils feel known and encouraged, they flourish, not just academically, but as individuals.
Outside of school, I am a mum to three boys, two of whom are now grown up and independent, which gives me a real appreciation of how quickly children grow and how important these early school years are.
Since I joined Devonshire House in September, I had the pleasure to meet all the pupils, staff, and families. My priorities as a new Head of School is to get to know the community and start building the strong relationships that are at the heart of this happy and successful school.
© Devonshire House 2026
The best way to get to know our school is to visit one of our Open Mornings!

Football at the heart of school life
A full-time Tottenham Hotspur Football Development coach is embedded into our curriculum, bringing professional-level football training to pupils at Devonshire House School.
What this means for our pupils
Support at fixtures and tournaments
Inclusivity and sporting excellence
The programme is open to all pupils, with dedicated football development pathways for both girls and boys, building on the school’s strong tradition of inclusivity and sporting excellence.
“We’re proud to offer every pupil – whether they play for fun or show real promise – the chance to grow through football,” said Henry Keighley-Elstub, Headteacher of Devonshire House. “This partnership will bring professional coaching into our everyday school life and reflects our belief in sport’s role in building confidence, resilience and teamwork.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Work | Devonshire House Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) Framework
Nursery is all about creating solid foundations for your child, the building block on which the rest of their education will lie. Our key objective is to switch on your child’s love of learning through experiencing success.
Child-initiated learning
Our carefully scaffolded, play-based, hands-on approach focuses on the 3 prime areas of learning and development required to form the bedrock for future learning.
We teach these 3 prime areas of learning through:
Yes, we are a nursery school, but there’s no point in being able to write your name if you can’t sit next to someone and ask for a pen; the underlying developmental areas must be secure for your child to fulfil their potential later.
We have seen great progress in our daughter’s numeracy and writing, although she remains convinced that “nursery is only for playing and chatting to my friend” – Mum of Elizabeth in Oaks
Communications & language development
Personal, social & emotional development
Physical development
Literacy
Mathematics
Understanding the world
Expressive arts & design
We balance adult-directed teaching and child-initiated learning
We will get to know your child so that we can build on their interests, likes and needs, in order for them to progress in each area.
© Devonshire House 2026
The best way to get to know our school is to visit one of our Open Mornings!

Why speaking a second language?
In today’s increasingly interdependent world, speaking a second language is an essential skill that allows your child to communicate and connect with others. The advantages of language learning are well documented. It can boost creativity, build confidence & self-esteem, stimulate brain development and help your child better understand their first language.
Engagement & Creativity
French is generously timetabled right from Nursery. The focus is on engagement and creativity. We want your child to enjoy languages and be willing to have a go. Think interactive puppetry and songs, cheese tasting and cross curricular input, such as PE and Drama in French.
Once your child has developed a good ear & accent from lots of speaking and listening, we move to the written form but always with enjoyment in mind. Knowledge is consolidated by experiences such as workshops and celebration of key dates in the calendar. If French is your child’s mother tongue, they can join our bilingual club.
© Devonshire House 2026
The best way to get to know our school is to visit one of our Open Mornings!

pageCache.pageTitle: STEM Learning | Devonshire House Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Importance of Science & Technology
Advances in science & technology are changing our societal landscape on a seemingly daily basis. If we are to succeed in equipping your child to navigate their future, a strong grounding in STEM subjects is paramount.
Science
We teach your child to be a confident and enthusiastic scientist. We give your child the skills they need to tackle new scientific topics armed with confident critical thinking skills, an understanding of scientific methods and intellectual curiosity for what they will learn.
Science is taught as one subject to Year 6, and then split into Biology, Chemistry & Physics from Year 7. We enrich the curriculum with activities designed to engage your child and cement our position as a community leader in inspiring science:
Daily inspiring science videos
Technology
Your child is likely to have a job that doesn’t yet exist. It will almost certainly require fluency with technology in some form. Our role is to equip your child with the skills to navigate their technological future, whatever that may look like.
For that reason, our IT curriculum is far from standard. As well as teaching the computation skills, digital literacy, computer science, programming and app / game development skills required to take GCSE and A Level at senior school, we focus on the softer skills required to be discerning and competent users.
Your child might come home and talk about the risks they need to consider about new technologies such as AI. They might tell you about malware – the laws, the risks and the measures required to stay safe online. Whatever your personal views on screens, technology is accessible 24/7 and it’s important your child is equipped to use it to their advantage for their learning and for life.
© Devonshire House 2026
The best way to get to know our school is to visit one of our Open Mornings!

pageCache.pageTitle: The Arts | Devonshire House Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Finding their spark
Our mission to grow upstanding people, equipped to navigate their future and alive to their talents and passions requires a holistic education. One which embraces all the many developmental benefits The Arts bring.
Visual arts
Art is for everyone at Devonshire House. We want your child to learn to express themselves creatively using a variety of forms, building fine motor skills along the way:
From Year 4, your child will have specialist teaching weekly in the art room. Lessons intentionally link to topics they are studying in other subjects, enriching understanding and broadening students’ knowledge. For example, while we paint the animals studied in science, we also learn about watercolour techniques and famous watercolour artists, tying science, art history and art techniques together.
The visual arts provision is enhanced by a range of enrichment opportunities:
Painting
3D sculpture
Print making
Art clubs
Trips to galleries
Music
Your child will have weekly, specialist led, class music lessons from as young as Nursery.
Unlike many prep schools, we offer 1-1 lessons on most orchestral instruments, meaning your child is as likely to learn the French horn, saxophone or oboe as the more traditional piano, violin & flute. Trial sessions are available to help your child find the right instrument for them.
Music is for sharing, which explains our emphasis on providing your child with live music making opportunities:
From an early age, your child will practise performing in front of an audience in assemblies, gaining the confidence for bigger audiences such as:
If your child shows musical promise and talent, they may be awarded one of our internal music scholarships in Year 3. These bring both financial benefit and an ambassadorial role. Scholars are role models for younger children, buddying them and encouraging them to take part in concerts, sowing the seeds for music for life. We also prepare children for Music Scholarships to senior schools.
Junior Orchestra (Years 1-2)
Chamber Orchestra (Years 3-8)
Jazz band
Woodwind group
String ensemble.
Tea concerts
Singing for the local community
Music jamborees
Carol services
Prize day
Charity choral performances in London venues
Drama
Drama provides an important creative stimulus away from the academic rigour of the classroom. It builds confidence, promotes teamwork, and is a wonderful way to learn about yourself and others.
Your child will have annual opportunities to be on the stage and experience the full range of human emotions performance can bring – excitement, nerves, pride and elation. From Nursery to Year 3, this takes the form of Christmas productions. Your child will be able to take part in a range of performances, as well as regular whole-school productions held off-site at The Tabernacle Theatre.
Our focus on inclusivity means your child will doubtless join many generations before in demonstrating a real appetite to contribute to our productions in some guise. All talents are promoted and celebrated, from the talented drummer who doesn’t want to say anything, to the artist who makes mind-blowing props to the eagle-eyed reader who prompts when memories falter.
© Devonshire House 2026
The best way to get to know our school is to visit one of our Open Mornings!

pageCache.pageTitle: Outdoor Play | Devonshire House Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
The outdoor benefits
The benefits of outdoor learning are well documented, which is why we invest as heavily in our outdoor learning environment as our indoor spaces. Your child’s gross motor skills will be supported by the climbing frame and pirate ship, and there’s messy play aplenty in the mud kitchen and sandpits.
The outdoor learning area encourages collaboration and imagination, giving your child the confidence to take risks in a safe environment. A covered area allows your child to get out whatever the weather.
From Oaks, in the Summer Term, your child will also benefit from weekly Forest School sessions on the neighbouring Lower School site.
© Devonshire House 2026
The best way to get to know our school is to visit one of our Open Mornings!

We come together
Much as we hope your child will sail smoothly through childhood without a glitch, storms can hit unexpectedly. We partner with you thoughtfully and deliberately to ensure that we support your child and meet their needs throughout their time with us.
Form teachers
Your first point of call with any worries is always your child’s form teacher, who knows them best. The Deputy Head (pastoral) has overall responsibility for wellbeing and knows all the children very well. Together, we work as a team to put in place the right support to help your child through their struggles.
What does that support look like?
No two situations are ever the same, but we have a range of proactive tools and people at our disposal:
Modern Approach to Therapy with Terapia
Professional psychotherapists from the organisation Terapia use in-depth counselling skills and non-verbal techniques such as art, play, drama and music therapies in one-to-one sessions to enable children to express themselves, work through difficulties, release anxiety and improve their self-esteem.
Our partner therapists are at the school four days a week to support our children during one-to-one or group sessions.
Staff members and parents are encouraged to refer the children to our Learning Support Team who will work with Terapia to decide on the best approach to support the children in need.
Therapy sessions are held in a supportive, safe and warm space involving play, talking and creativity.
Terapia also offers parenting sessions – from three to twelve 50-minutes sessions per parent.
Finally, professionals at Terapia are working along with the Learning Support and the Senior Leadership teams to hold themed group sessions and workshops on common themes.
Tooled Up Partnership
Parenting is a journey and no-one would ever set off on a journey without some tools, ideas and strategies for navigating the path ahead. Our school aims to ensure that all parents and carers have full access to a digital platform that ensures you are staying up to date with modern-day parenting and that you have access to actionable ideas derived from the highest quality research evidence.
Tooled Up is curated by one of the UK’s leading experts on parental engagement in children’s lives and learning.
© Devonshire House 2026
The best way to get to know our school is to visit one of our Open Mornings!

School Holidays Camps
Let’s Leap transforms school holidays into action-packed playgrounds! With over 50 activities like archery, go-karting, arts and crafts, multi-sports, and inflatable obstacle courses, children are in for epic adventures! Let’s Leap team ensures a safe, thrilling experience for children aged 3 to 13.
Familiar and trusting environment
Your child can have fun with their friends, in a familiar and trusted setting. Let’s Leap provides safe, supportive childcare that builds confidence and keeps children active and engaged all week long with exciting activities.
Flexible Childcare
Join in for a day or the whole week! With flexible options to fit your family schedule:
Standard Day: 8:30 am – 4:30 pm
Extended Day: 8:00 am – 5:30 pm

WOW Activities
This is not just about the classics — Let’s Leap Holiday Camps feature incredible extras like electric bumper cars, Segway training, drone flying, electric go-karting, zorb football, laser tag, and animal shows — all at no extra cost!
Here’s just a taste of what’s waiting for your child:
🏎️ Electric Segway Go-Karting 🤺 Fencing 🎾 Multi-Sports 🎯 Nerf Tag
And that’s just the beginning! There’s plenty more to explore:
🎨 Arts & Crafts 🏹 Archery 🎉 Team Games 🏰 Bouncy Castles
Operational Dates

For more information about Let’s Leap Holiday Camps and how to register and book, please visit our website:
You can contact them at milo@letsleap.co.uk.

A wide range of Senior schools for all
The many excellent senior schools to which our pupils progress – including South Hampstead High School, UCS, Highgate, St Paul’s School, Channing, Francis Holland Regent’s Park, Merchant Taylors’ School, Wetherby Senior and Mill Hill School – and the broad array of scholarships awarded to them each year, demonstrate our commitment to equipping your child to navigate their future in the school where they will best fit and flourish.

Senior Schools Results Year 6 – 4-Year Trend Including 2025-2026
Year 6 Senior Schools Destinations – 2025-2026
More on Senior School Results for Devonshire House Year 8 Cohort (13+):
Senior Schools Results Year 8 – 3-Year Trend Including 2024-2025
The Dukes Village
Devonshire House is part of the Dukes Education family of schools and educators, brought together by a common purpose: to give children the foundations for an extraordinary life.
We create clusters of nurseries and schools in village locations to ensure that families can enjoy the option of an all-through education journey with Dukes Education within their local area.
Continuity and Confidence
As students prepare to transition from prep school to senior school, our guaranteed entry policy offers a seamless progression within the Dukes family of senior schools, subject only to the availability of a place and a child’s ability to thrive in the ethos and curriculum, and without the need to sit traditional school entrance exams such as the 11+ or 13+.
Guaranteed Placement, Tailored Support
Dukes Education supports each child’s journey to senior school, working with families to find the right school; one that matches their unique strengths and aspirations.
Our commitment to providing a guaranteed place at a Dukes Education senior school allows students to focus on their personal and academic development instead of spending precious time preparing for school entrance exams and the added pressure that entails.
For families applying to selective senior schools, our prep schools provide thorough guidance, tailored 11+ and 13+ exam preparation and exceptional pastoral support to ensure that every student is ready to perform at their best.
This approach ensures a confident and smooth transition to senior school for all children, nurturing lifelong learners within the supportive framework of Dukes Education.
Early acceptance
If a family decides their child will not sit the 11+ or 13+ entrance test, we are usually able to confirm acceptance to a Dukes senior school, for example, in Year 5. Early acceptance offers families peace of mind, allowing children to enjoy their final years at prep school and focus on a positive transition to senior school.
Hampstead Fine Arts College
Hampstead Fine Arts College
Mrs Candida Cave Principal https://www.hampsteadfinearts.com/ Ages 13-18
Hampstead Fine Arts College is a leading independent school in North London, specialising in the Arts and Humanities for students aged 13-19. Nestled in Hampstead, the college provides a unique environment where creativity and individuality thrive. Small class sizes and a personalised approach combine academic rigour with artistic freedom, fostering confidence, independence, and intellectual curiosity. With strong pastoral care and a supportive community, Fine Arts College empowers students to excel both artistically and academically, preparing them for future studies and creative careers.
London Park School, Mayfair
London Park School, Mayfair
Dr Adrian Rainbow Headteacher www.londonparkschools.com/mayfair Ages 11-16
Situated in iconic Piccadilly within a beautiful Grade I listed building by Robert Adam, LPS Mayfair (formerly Eaton Square Senior) blends historical charm with modern learning. Just a short walk from London’s renowned galleries, museums, and theatres, the school makes the most of the city’s rich cultural resources. Deliberately small, LPS Mayfair fosters a close-knit community where each student is nurtured, challenged, and supported to achieve their best. After completing GCSEs, students move on to LPS Sixth, a sixth form centre located near Victoria station.
© Devonshire House 2026
The best way to get to know our school is to visit one of our Open Mornings!

Devonshire House Prep School Open Days
Come and discover our school for yourself. Our Open Mornings are the best way to see Devonshire House in action and a unique opportunity to meet our Head, SLT members and admissions members at the same time, as well as hear directly from the pupils.
Autumn Term 2026 Open Morning Dates
Thursday 8 October 2026
Thursday 5 November 2026
Thursday 26 November 2026
Open Mornings run every 3–4 weeks during term time – register your interest and we’ll let you know about future dates too.
Autumn Term 2026
"*" indicates required fields
What happens at an Open Morning?
After a brief introduction from our Head of School, our Upper School pupils (Year 6 to 8) will be your tour guides and take you to our different campuses. They can describe our school life and answer your questions better than anyone else!
After your tour (bespoke to your child’s year of entry), you will have the opportunity to stay for a Q&A session with our Senior Leadership and Admissions teams.
What to Expect on the Morning
09:00–09:15 – Arrival and refreshments
09:15–09:30 – Welcome from the Head
Good to Know Before You Visit
Should I bring my child to an Open Morning?
Yes, children are very welcome. Buggies aren’t used during the tour itself and are left in the hall.
Is there parking at Devonshire House?
There’s no parking on-site, though nearby street parking is usually available. We’re close to Hampstead and Finchley Road underground stations.
What happens if I need to cancel?
Just email admissions@dhprep.co.uk to let us know and we’ll release your place.
How do I register?
Book online via the registration form on this page – you’ll receive an automated confirmation email.
How long will the event last?
Tours will finish at 10.30. After that you’re welcome to stay for an optional Q&A session with members of the Leadership and Admissions teams. If you need to leave before 10.30, please let your tour guide know at the start of the tour.
© Devonshire House 2026

pageCache.text:
Frequently Asked Questions
How is the Devonshire House provision different from daycare?
At Devonshire House, we provide a nurturing environment to support the ever-changing needs of the developing two-year old children. Our aim is to support each child as they gain independence. Initially our focus is on personal care and forming strong relationships. Gradually, we enable your child to grow and develop a love of learning that will last throughout their time at Devonshire House.
What hours do you do?
In Acorns Nursery (age 2), our School day starts at 08:30 and finishes at 15:00, or 12:00 if you have opted for a Morning Session.
In Oaks Nursery (age 3), our School day starts at 09:00 and finishes at 15:00, with doors opening at 08:00.
Our after-school care is provided by our partner ‘Let’s Leap’ for both year groups, and gives you options to opt in or out on a daily basis, as well as to pick-up your child at any time until 18:00.
What is your staff member to child ratio?
For children aged 2 years old, we endeavour to maintain a ratio of 1 qualified adult for 4 children.
Please note that the official ratio, as outlined by the Early Years Foundation Stage, is 1 qualified adult for 5 children at 2 years old.
For children aged 3 to 4 years old, we ensure a ratio of 1 qualified adult for 8 children.
What meals and snacks are provided?
At School, we provide a morning snack with a selection of fruits and breadsticks.
At lunch time, Nursery children join their friends in the Hall and eat homemade meals prepared onsite by our Chef, varied throughout the week with healthy portions of meet, vegetables and fresh fruits for dessert, served by our Nursery staff members, who also supervise them throughout the lunch time.
All allergies are catered for.
Can my child sleep at Nursery?
In Acorns (age 2), we cater for a 2-hour long nap in the afternoon. Children can sleep as little or as long as they want after their lunch until 2pm.
In Oaks (age 3), children won’t have the opportunity to nap but instead, we initiate a ‘calm’ time in our wellbeing corner every day after lunch.
Do children need to be toilet-trained when joining the Nursery?
For entry to Acorns (age 2), we do not expect children to be toilet-trained as we have changing rooms onsite and experienced staff members.
For entry to Oaks (age 3), we ask all children to be toilet-trained before joining. Please note that age-appropriate toilets are easily accessible for each Oaks class.
Do you have Key Workers?
In Acorns (age 2), each child is allocated a Key Person to take care of them (changing their nappies, helping them settling in the morning, taking care of their belongings…) The Key Person forms strong bonds with the child – especially during the settling period. As the child becomes more familiar and comfortable at school, they end to form equally strong bonds with all staff.
In Oaks (age 3), each class has a class teacher and a dedicated teaching assistant.
Is there an automatic transition to the School after the Nursery?
After completing their second year of Nursery (Oaks class), children benefit from a priority place to join our School in Reception, until the end of Year 6 or the end of Year 8.
No assessment is needed, however, due to high interest from prospective parents in Reception places each year, we kindly ask Nursery parents in the Spring Term to reserve a place for their child in Devonshire House Reception.

Inspiring a love of learning
Our open, light and airy classrooms as well as our high staff: pupil ratios ensure that your child’s unique and natural talents are recognised and encouraged from the moment they start.
The Nursery team, teachers and support staff are highly qualified and dedicated to infusing every learning moment with fun and inspiration. They span extremely experienced teachers with master’s degrees, to newly qualified professionals full of exciting ideas which enrich our pedagogy.
Our aim is to give your child the best introduction to school life and build a love of learning that will last them throughout Devonshire House and beyond.
A home-from-home nursery school
At Devonshire House home-from-home means getting to know you and your child, and doing all we can to make you both feel comfortable and at ease.
It is ringing you to let you know they’ve settled after a wobbly drop off and are busy chatting to you on a wooden block held to their ear. Home-from-home is stroking your child’s hair at nap time because that’s what they need to get to sleep. Home-from-home ensures that your child has the food they like, on a plate they like. It is setting out your child’s favourite farm animals before they arrive in the morning.
Home from home is natural, uncluttered spaces with fewer high-quality items. It is bespoke, caring and nurturing.
Why does home-from home matter?
If your child feels at home, they will skip into school in the morning. And if they are happy at school, the rest will follow. Home-from-home is the basis for effective learning. It is the magic ingredient that allows your child to feel safe, known and loved which in turn fosters curiosity, exploration, endeavour and independence. Home-from-home also enables us to partner successfully with you. It keeps the communication lines open to prevent issues from festering and to share celebratory moments.
We’d love to welcome you. Come to an Open Morning and see if Devonshire House feels like your child’s home-from-home.
